subject: Runway extension + thermostat-scaling amendment request
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma@brightpath.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected peak — request for temporary runway and thermostat scaling

Hi Naomi / Ben,

Quick note from our ops team: we saw a 3x spike in inference throughput last week (attached summary) tied to a marketing test. The current Dedicated commitment is hitting headroom and request latency is creeping into our P95 SLA.

We don't want to change the committed tranche long-term yet — product usage is experimental — but we need a short-term operational hedge while we validate the test. Two asks:

1) A 6-week runway extension (grace top-up) to give us breathing room for the test.
2) Enable the "thermostat" scaling mode you mentioned in the kickoff (automated baseline thermostat that adds short-lived capacity once utilization crosses thresholds). We want the thermostat to kick in only for bursts >30% above normal runrate and cap at +20 GPUs.

Can you share cost impact, amendment language, and the telemetry we'd see in the Console? We can sign a short addendum if the terms are straightforward.

Thanks — Emma
Emma Li
VP Operations, BrightPath AI

Attachments: usage-weekly-20261101.csv (summary), ops-incident-log.txt (referenced)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected peak — request for temporary runway and thermostat scaling

Emma — thanks for the heads up and for the attachments. We dug into the CSV and confirmed the spike aligns with the marketing window you called out. Proposed approach below:

Option A — Short addendum (recommended):
- 6-week burst window (2026-11-08 -> 2026-12-20) that increases your reserved capacity by up to 20 GPUs as needed.
- Thermostat mode enabled with these params: trigger = sustained 30% above 7-day rolling baseline for >10 minutes; cooldown = 15 minutes; max burst = +20 GPUs.
- Billing: burst GPUs billed at the dedicated hourly top-up rate (pro-rated) with a 10% premium on token units during burst windows (to reflect on-demand overhead). Estimated incremental cost: ~$12,400 for the full 6 weeks at current observed peak (see attached thermostat-config-proposal.pdf).

Option B — Commit amendment (if you want price smoothing): convert +20 GPUs into a temporary tranche at a discounted committed rate for the 6-week period. This lowers unit price but requires approval from Finance and changes the contract.

Observability: Console will show a new "Thermostat activity" row in the per-route dashboard with: trigger times, GPUs added, cost per burst minute, and a downloadable CSV. We'll also add an automated Slack alert to your ops channel when the thermostat engages.

I've attached a draft of the amendment (amendment-draft.docx) with Option A language filled in. Ben / Soojin — can you confirm the pricing calc and whether we need legal review for the short addendum?

If this looks good to Emma, we can push the addendum through DocuSign and enable thermostat in the Dedicated runtime with a feature-flag so it can be toggled on/off without a deploy.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Attachments: thermostat-config-proposal.pdf, amendment-draft.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Emma Li <emma@brightpath.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected peak — request for temporary runway and thermostat scaling

Naomi / Emma — confirmed on pricing. Calculation summary: 20 GPUs x average hourly burst utilization (estimated 6 hours/day) x 42 days x top-up rate = ~$11,200. Adding the platform overhead premium and anticipated token inflation brings the estimate to Naomi's ~$12.4k.

Legal: short addendum (Option A) is straightforward — we can encode the thermostat as an "Operational Burst Addendum" with the trigger/cooldown/max_gpus parameters enumerated and an explicit end date. I'll prep a one-paragraph approval note for Legal (no change to baseline SLA).

Operational note: recommend enabling thermostat in a dry-run mode for 48 hours (no billing) to verify thresholds. If telemetry looks good, flip to live billing. This mitigates surprise charges to BrightPath while we validate.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Emma Li <emma@brightpath.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, ops@brightpath.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 16:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected peak — request for temporary runway and thermostat scaling

Thanks everyone — that sounds reasonable. Two quick confirmations:

1) We accept Option A as drafted with the dry-run clause (48 hours no-bill thermostat verification).
2) Please send the DocuSign link for the Operational Burst Addendum and toggle the thermostat flag in dry-run mode on Monday.

Once we get the DocuSign completed, ops will monitor triggers and we'll coordinate a go/no-go at the end of the dry-run window. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Emma
VP Operations, BrightPath AI

Attachments: signed-internal-authorization.pdf (internal approval)
